en: My order was supposed to arrive yesterday.
tamil: என் ஆர்டர் நேத்தே வந்திருக்கணும்.
context: Complaining about a late delivery.
explain: 'Was supposed to' means something was planned but did not happen.
usage: Use it with customer care when your parcel is late.
leelaQ: Has an order of yours ever come late?
answer: Yes, my phone arrived three days late once.

en: Can you tell me where my parcel is now?
tamil: என் பார்சல் இப்ப எங்க இருக்குன்னு சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: Asking customer care about a parcel.
explain: 'Can you tell me' is a polite way to ask for information. Then the word order is normal: 'where my parcel is'.
usage: Use it on a customer care call or chat about a delayed parcel.
leelaQ: How do you find out where your parcel is?
answer: I open the app and check the tracking page.

en: I ordered a phone cover online last night.
tamil: நேத்து ராத்திரி ஆன்லைன்ல போன் கவர் ஆர்டர் பண்ணினேன்.
context: Telling someone about an online purchase.
explain: 'Ordered' is the past of 'order'. 'Online' means on the internet.
usage: Use it in casual talk or when you start a complaint.
leelaQ: What do you buy online most often?
answer: I buy books and phone accessories online.

en: The delivery boy called me, but I could not hear him.
tamil: டெலிவரி பையன் போன் பண்ணினான், ஆனா எனக்கு கேட்கல.
context: Explaining a missed delivery call.
explain: 'Could not' is the negative past of 'can'. 'But' shows a problem.
usage: Use it when you explain why you missed a delivery.
leelaQ: What do you do when you miss a delivery call?
answer: I call back the delivery boy at once.

en: Please leave the parcel with the security guard.
tamil: பார்சலை செக்யூரிட்டிகிட்ட கொடுத்துட்டு போங்க.
context: Giving delivery instructions.
explain: 'Leave it with' means give it to someone to keep. 'Please' makes it polite.
usage: Use it when you are not at home and the delivery person calls.
leelaQ: Who receives parcels when you are out?
answer: My neighbour or the security guard receives them.

en: The app shows that my order is out for delivery.
tamil: என் ஆர்டர் டெலிவரிக்கு கிளம்பிடுச்சுன்னு ஆப்ல காட்டுது.
context: Telling family the order status.
explain: 'Out for delivery' means the parcel has left the warehouse. 'Shows that' introduces the news.
usage: Use it to tell your family to expect a parcel today.
leelaQ: How do you know when your parcel will come?
answer: The app sends me a message with the time.

en: How long will it take to deliver to Madurai?
tamil: மதுரைக்கு டெலிவரி பண்ண எவ்வளவு நாள் ஆகும்?
context: Asking a seller about delivery time.
explain: 'How long will it take' asks for the time needed. 'To deliver to' gives the place.
usage: Use it when you order from a seller in another city.
leelaQ: Do you like fast delivery or cheap delivery?
answer: I prefer cheap delivery if I am not in a hurry.

en: I have been waiting for the courier since morning.
tamil: நான் காலையிலேர்ந்து கூரியருக்காக காத்திருக்கேன்.
context: Complaining about a long wait.
explain: 'Have been waiting' with 'since morning' shows the wait is still going on.
usage: Use it when you call to find out why the courier has not come.
leelaQ: Have you ever waited a long time for something?
answer: Yes, I waited two hours for a courier last month.

en: Do you offer cash on delivery?
tamil: கேஷ் ஆன் டெலிவரி இருக்கா?
context: Asking a seller about payment options.
explain: 'Cash on delivery' means you pay when the parcel comes. 'Do you offer' asks if a service is given.
usage: Use it when you order from a small seller online.
leelaQ: Do you prefer to pay before or after delivery?
answer: I prefer to pay after delivery, so I feel safe.

en: I will track my order using this link.
tamil: இந்த லிங்கை வெச்சு என் ஆர்டரை டிராக் பண்ணுவேன்.
context: Telling the seller you will check the status.
explain: 'Using this link' tells the method. 'Track' means to follow the movement of a parcel.
usage: Use it after the seller sends a tracking link.
leelaQ: What information do you check while tracking?
answer: I check the date and the delivery city.

en: The product I received is different from the photo.
tamil: நான் வாங்கின பொருள் போட்டோவுல இருக்கிறதுல இருந்து வித்தியாசமா இருக்கு.
context: Complaining about a wrong product.
explain: 'Is different from' compares two things. 'I received' tells which product.
usage: Use it in a complaint to the seller or the app support.
leelaQ: What do you do when the product looks different?
answer: I take a photo and send it to the customer care.

en: Could you send me the tracking number again?
tamil: டிராக்கிங் நம்பரை திரும்ப அனுப்ப முடியுமா?
context: Asking a seller for the number.
explain: 'Could you' is polite. 'Again' means one more time.
usage: Use it in a message to a seller when you lose the number.
leelaQ: Where do you keep important order details?
answer: I keep them in my email and in my phone.

en: Free delivery is available for orders above five hundred rupees.
tamil: ஐநூறு ரூபாய்க்கு மேல ஆர்டர் பண்ணா டெலிவரி இலவசம்.
context: Explaining a shop's delivery rule.
explain: 'Available for' tells who can use the offer. 'Above' means more than.
usage: Use it when you tell a friend how to save on delivery charges.
leelaQ: How do you save money when you shop online?
answer: I add more items to my cart to get free delivery.

en: I always read the reviews before buying anything online.
tamil: ஆன்லைன்ல எதையும் வாங்கறதுக்கு முன்னாடி நான் எப்பவும் ரிவ்யூ படிப்பேன்.
context: Talking about a safe shopping habit.
explain: 'Before buying' is used with -ing. 'Always' shows a regular habit.
usage: Use it when you give shopping advice to a friend.
leelaQ: Why are reviews useful?
answer: They tell us if the product is good or bad.

en: My package has not arrived yet.
tamil: என் பேக்கேஜ் இன்னும் வரல.
context: Telling support the parcel is missing.
explain: 'Has not arrived yet' shows something expected has not happened until now.
usage: Use it when you contact the seller about a late order.
leelaQ: What will you say to the seller about a late parcel?
answer: I will say that my package has not arrived yet.

en: Please call me before you come, I may be outside.
tamil: வர்றதுக்கு முன்னாடி போன் பண்ணுங்க, நான் வெளியே இருக்கலாம்.
context: Asking the delivery person to call first.
explain: 'Before you come' gives the time. 'May be' shows it is possible.
usage: Use it when you give instructions to a delivery person.
leelaQ: When do you ask a delivery person to call?
answer: I ask them to call when I am at work.

en: I am adding these two items to my cart.
tamil: இந்த ரெண்டு பொருளையும் என் கார்ட்டுல சேர்க்கிறேன்.
context: Describing what you do on a shopping app.
explain: 'Am adding' shows an action happening now. 'Cart' is the basket on a shopping website.
usage: Use it when you shop online with a friend and explain your steps.
leelaQ: What items are in your cart now?
answer: I have a pair of earphones and a book in my cart.

en: Is the delivery charge included in this price?
tamil: டெலிவரி சார்ஜ் இந்த விலையில சேர்த்தா?
context: Asking if the price has extra charges.
explain: 'Included in' means already part of the price. It avoids a surprise at the end.
usage: Use it when you order from a seller by phone or chat.
leelaQ: Do hidden charges bother you?
answer: Yes, I do not like surprise charges at the end.

en: The festival sale starts at midnight.
tamil: பண்டிகை சேல் நள்ளிரவு பன்னிரண்டு மணிக்கு ஆரம்பிக்குது.
context: Telling a friend about a sale time.
explain: The simple present is used for fixed events like a sale time. 'Midnight' is twelve at night.
usage: Use it around Diwali or Pongal when online sales begin.
leelaQ: Do you shop during festival sales?
answer: Yes, I buy clothes for the family during festival sales.

en: Don't forget to rate the seller after delivery.
tamil: டெலிவரிக்கு அப்புறம் விற்பனையாளருக்கு ரேட்டிங் கொடுக்க மறக்காதீங்க.
context: Reminding a family member.
explain: 'Don't forget to' is a common reminder. 'Rate' means to give stars.
usage: Use it when you remind a friend or relative after they shop online.
leelaQ: Do you give ratings after a delivery?
answer: Yes, I give a rating if the service is good.

en: They said I will get the refund in seven days.
tamil: ஏழு நாள்ல ரீஃபண்ட் கிடைக்கும்னு சொன்னாங்க.
context: Reporting what customer care said.
explain: 'They said' reports someone's words. 'Will get' talks about a promise for the future.
usage: Use it when you tell someone what support told you.
leelaQ: How long does a refund take usually?
answer: It usually takes about a week.

en: Which coupon code should I use for this order?
tamil: இந்த ஆர்டருக்கு எந்த கூப்பன் கோடு யூஸ் பண்ணணும்?
context: Asking a friend about a discount code.
explain: 'Which' is used when there are a few choices. 'Should' asks for advice.
usage: Use it when you shop online and need a friend's advice on discounts.
leelaQ: Do you use coupon codes when you shop?
answer: Yes, I search for a coupon code before I pay.

en: My cousin returned the shoes because they were too small.
tamil: என் cousin ஷூவை ரொம்ப சின்னதா இருந்ததால திருப்பி கொடுத்தான்.
context: Telling why someone returned a product.
explain: 'Because' gives the reason. 'Too small' means smaller than needed.
usage: Use it when you talk about online shopping problems.
leelaQ: Why do people return things they order online?
answer: They return things because the size or colour is wrong.

en: Could you deliver it after six in the evening?
tamil: சாயந்திரம் ஆறு மணிக்கு மேல டெலிவரி பண்ண முடியுமா?
context: Asking the delivery person for a time.
explain: 'Could you' makes the request polite. 'After six' gives the time limit.
usage: Use it when you are at work during the day.
leelaQ: What time are you free to receive a parcel?
answer: I am free after six in the evening.

en: I saved a lot of money during the sale.
tamil: சேல்ல நிறைய பணம் மிச்சம் பண்ணினேன்.
context: Sharing a good shopping result.
explain: 'Saved' is the past of 'save'. 'A lot of' means much.
usage: Use it when you tell friends about a good deal.
leelaQ: How much did you save last time?
answer: I saved almost five hundred rupees on a bag.
